rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you for the offer—I really appreciated meeting you too. Five hours a week of data analysis support would be incredibly valuable. Here's what I'm working on: I'm exploring whether Halcyon Threshold should focus on independent evaluations of frontier model safety capabilities—specifically, developing and publishing rigorous evals on safety-relevant behaviors that models might demonstrate but that aren't being systematically measured. Would you be interested in helping with data analysis and visualization around this? I'd want to pull together existing work, identify gaps, and potentially coordinate with other independent evals practitioners. Your skillset would be perfect for organizing and analyzing the landscape. Can we set up a brief call this week to discuss? Thanks, Morgan"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: CONFIRMED (5 hrs/week, data analysis)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "Exploring frontier model evals collaboration". It read: "Hi Sam, I'm developing Halcyon Threshold's initial focus and I keep coming back to the observation that frontier model evaluation is chronically underfunded and mostly happens inside labs. I'm exploring whether we could organize independent evaluation efforts—developing, coordinating, and publishing rigorous evals on safety-relevant model behaviors that aren't being systematically measured outside the labs. Given your work on independent evals, I'm wondering: 1. What do you see as the biggest gaps in what's being evaluated? 2. Is this a space where you'd be interested in collaborating or where more funding/coordination would actually help? 3. Are there 2-3 other people you'd recommend I talk to about this? Happy to do a call if that's easier. Best, Morgan"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tomasz Wrona <twrona@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Question on evals and governance approaches". It read: "Hi Tomasz, I'm thinking through what Halcyon Threshold should focus on. I keep coming back to the thought that independent evaluation of frontier models is a critical but underfunded piece of the governance puzzle—you can't govern what you don't measure. From your governance angle, what do you see as the biggest gaps? Is this something you see as important to the governance agenda? Curious for your perspective. Best, Morgan"
